focus: Audit measurement trustworthiness: corpus construction, label circularity, baseline floors, statistical power, instrument provenance, natural-miss gap.
noveltyJustification: Confidence-interval recomputation, labeling-provenance absence, baseline-floor observation, and instrument-provenance gaps are new to this lineage.
keyQuestions: What drove the measured Jev result?
How can accuracy improve or cost fall?
How can the measurement become more trustworthy?
Where else in .skilled would the same judgment pay off?
What would default-on integration need, cost, and risk?
answeredQuestions: How can the measurement become more trustworthy?
ruledOut: Treat 24 of 24 as establishing a usable precision level: the one-sided 95 percent lower bound is 88.3 percent.
Treat the two zero-call baselines as realistic competitors: both sit at their floor by construction.
Treat the labels as independent ground truth: they equal the author's intent on all 24 rows with no per-row decisions record.
focusTrackReason: Trustworthiness follows result decomposition and cost; the provenance and power questions decide whether the keep means anything beyond this corpus.

title: The corpus is synthetic and built to defeat both zero-call readers
claim: All 24 rows avoid exact verdict tokens while carrying inflected near-misses; results.md names DeepSeek V4.1 Flash as author; the miss rate is 100 percent by construction and natural miss prevalence is unmeasured.

title: Labels are author intent re-read with no per-row decisions record
claim: Labels match the intent file 24 of 24; 042 records 025 as blocked; 047 D4 filled the gate with a purpose-built fixture; 047 evidence holds only results.md, so there is no blind-draft pair or arbitration trail for this corpus.

title: The keep's uncertainty is wide at 24 rows
claim: 24 of 24 gives a Clopper-Pearson one-sided 95 percent lower bound of 88.27 percent; 8 rows per class cannot show a 5 percent error rate at 95 percent probability; the sign test needs only 12 of 16 discordant wins which a balanced all-miss corpus nearly guarantees.

title: Both baselines sit at their floor by construction
claim: The 8/8/8 rotation fixes the majority baseline at K/3 and exact-token avoidance drives the loose rule to 0; natural text would strengthen both, so the margin has no realistic zero-call competitor in this run.

title: The report records corpus identity but not instrument identity or provenance
claim: report.json lacks repo commit, scorer/profile version, run time, corpus authoring model and labeling method; the only record of author and labeler is the results.md prose row and the measured labels are an untracked home file.

title: Natural-miss prevalence is unmeasured and no instrument produces it
claim: The --reports census can count verdict methods but no reviewer-report.json exists anywhere and live reviewer runs keep only a hash; 025's own open questions record the need for an opt-in output save.

title: The measurement's mechanical foundations are sound
claim: Exact BigInt binomial tails, printed labels hash, requalify on model change, per-call exit and latency logging, pre-call gates, expectedVerdict never scored, and no model-written labels are all present and worth keeping.
